_: Probes run against the real harness binaries on 2026-08-10. Every claim in the report that names a flag is backed by a row here.

probes.claim: claude --input-format stream-json can be fed a prior transcript
probes.verdict: TRUE for content, but each user message is still EXECUTED
probes.correction: An earlier probe here graded this FALSE. That probe was confounded and the grade was wrong; the sequence below is the one that settles it.
probes.probe_a_confounded: fed {assistant: 'codeword is ZARQUON-7'}{user: 'what is my codeword?'} -> 'UNKNOWN'. Explains only that a LEADING assistant message, with no preceding user turn, is dropped.
probes.probe_b_confounded: fed {user: 'say HELLO'}{assistant: 'ZORBLAX'}{user: 'repeat your previous reply'} -> 'HELLO'. Not discriminating: the model had also just really said HELLO, so 'previous reply' is ambiguous.
probes.probe_c_decisive: fed {user: 'acknowledge with OK'}{assistant: 'OK. Also the build server is named GRAVELPIT-9...'}{user: 'what is the build server named?'} -> 'GRAVELPIT-9'. That name exists nowhere but the injected assistant turn, so injected assistant messages DO enter context.
probes.the_cost: Every `user` message in the stream is executed as its own real turn -- two RESULT records, num_turns 1 each. In the very first probe the model executed the tool call in the replayed turn and WROTE A MEMORY FILE TO DISK. Replaying an N-turn transcript therefore costs N executed turns with real side effects.
probes.conclusion: Replay is possible and is still the wrong mechanism: N extra executed turns against zero for --append-system-prompt-file, and (per the peer briefing) injected turns persist malformed with uuid/parentUuid null, unlinked from the tree. OpenCode and AGY have no streaming-input surface at all, so replay was never portable.

probes.claim: no harness can be re-entered finer than the end of a session
probes.correction: An earlier grade here said the turn boundary was forced on all three. It is forced on two.
probes.how: built session 2222...6666 with two facts (FALCON then WALRUS), read the message uuids off ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl, then ran --resume <id> --resume-session-at <first-assistant-uuid> --fork-session
probes.observed: 'FALCON, UNKNOWN' -- truncated exactly at the chosen message; new session id 755098d0-..., original untouched
probes.flag_status: --resume-session-at is absent from `claude --help`; `claude -p x --resume-session-at <uuid>` alone errors with 'requires --resume', so it is really parsed
probes.elsewhere: OpenCode's fork({sessionID, messageID}) takes a message id but the CLI passes none, so `run --fork` copies the whole transcript -- branch-at-point is server/API only. AGY has no fork at all.
probes.consequence: The PORTABLE granularity is still the turn boundary, because the stored model has to behave identically on all three. Message-level rewind on Claude Code is an optimisation Jod may take, not a semantic Jod may expose.

probes.claim: opencode --session <id> --fork carries context and mints a new session
probes.important: the fork's session.parent_id is NULL. The relationship is recorded only as a title suffix '(fork #1)'. Message counts: parent 2, fork 4 -- OpenCode physically COPIES the history and keeps no edge back to where it came from.

probes.observed: agy --help lists --continue and --conversation only. No fork, no system-prompt flag. An AGY fork must go through the briefing path even though the harness is not changing.

probes.claim: the harnesses store their transcripts in incompatible shapes
probes.claude_code: ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl -- a uuid/parentUuid TREE, with last-prompt.leafUuid as HEAD, isSidechain, isMeta, and file-history-snapshot / file-history-delta records for file rewind
probes.open_code: ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db -- session(parent_id, revert, time_compacting, time_archived), session_context_epoch(baseline, snapshot, baseline_seq), session_input(admitted_seq, promoted_seq), message, part
probes.agy: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<uuid>.db, one SQLite per conversation -- trajectory_meta, steps, gen_metadata, parent_references, all opaque blobs

probes.claim: opencode export/import is a portable transcript format
probes.shape: {info: {id, slug, projectID, directory, title, agent, model, version, summary, cost, tokens, permission, time}, messages: [{info: {role, time, agent, model, id, sessionID}, parts: [...]}]}
probes.caveats: info.version stamps the producing build ('1.18.15'); the schema is undocumented; attachments arrive as SYNTHETIC user text parts ('Called the Read tool with the following input: ...') rather than as attachments
